facts.label: Jardim com abelhas
facts.sub: Use there is e there are para dizer o que existe e is/are + -ing para o que acontece agora: There are bees everywhere. They’re collecting pollen.

facts.label: Existe
facts.sub: Para dizer o que existe, use there is com uma coisa e there are com muitas: There is a hive. There are bees. Na fala, there is vira there’s.

facts.label: Agora
facts.sub: Para dizer o que acontece agora, use am/is/are + verbo com -ing: They’re collecting pollen. It’s landing on the flower. Use as contrações they’re e it’s.

We say “There is bees”. → Falso (We say There are bees.)

pages.title: A bright garden · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a bright afternoon in a garden in Edinburgh. The air is warm and quiet. Pablo stands near a row of flowers. A soft buzz fills the air. His neighbor Zoe opens the gate. Pablo points to the flowers.
“Zoe, look at the flowers! There are bees everywhere.” says Pablo. “Wow! What are they doing?” says Zoe. “They’re collecting pollen. They’re working very hard.” says Pablo.

Com we, a forma base: make.

She ___ every day. → flies
He is ___ now. → landing
We ___ every day. → make

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: There are soa “dér-ar”. O -ing soa “in”: working soa “uérkin”. Na fala rápida, they’re working fica “dêr-uérkin”.
pages.tip: Compare bee e be: o som é igual, o sentido muda.

solo: Modele, peça repetição, depois uso livre.
group: Foco: there are, -ing. Diga working como “uérkin”.
Coro, depois um a um; ouça sem corrigir tudo.
extra90: Cada aluno grava um áudio de 10 segundos e compara com o modelo.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
